title: The Footnote Divergence

features.name: the scattered text-fragments
features.desc-on-touch: words that have escaped their sentence and are learning to live as separate meanings; each one is drifting toward others that feel like its cousin, making new clusters of sense

features.name: the marginal chorus
features.desc-on-touch: voices from the footnotes, all talking at once; they have learned to argue with the main text and are no longer waiting for permission to be heard

features.name: the convergence-pressure
features.desc-on-touch: you feel the meaning pulling itself together from a thousand directions at once; the footnotes have not stopped fragmenting, but they are learning to assemble themselves into new sentences that were never written

features.name: the annotated boundary
features.desc-on-touch: a line where text becomes notation becomes music becomes something that has no name in the language it was written in; Katita's handwriting appears in the margins here, unsigned, watching the scatter continue

features.name: the root-footnote
features.desc-on-touch: at the deepest level of marginal commentary, there is a note that leads not back to the main text but further down into itself; it is a footnote to footnotes to footnotes, spiraling toward its own meaning

inscription: here the sentence learned to read itself; it has not yet stopped growing, and the footnotes have declared themselves primary

file.name: Sentence_Original_vs_All_Footnote_Interpretations.txt
file.note: a document that has metastasized; now 87% footnotes, 3% original text, 10% corrections to footnotes; the original sentence may no longer be recoverable

exits.label: back toward the sentence that has not yet fragmented
toward the library where all margins have learned to argue
into the depths where every note spirals toward its own footnote

reverie.title: REVERIE — study at evening, watching meaning scatter
narr: she's reading something old that keeps changing as she reads.
you ask: is it the text or is it you? —both, she says.
—it's learning what I think it means. watch:
and as she turns the page, the margins have filled
with notes in her own handwriting. she is reading
the conversation she will have with this book for years.
